exposure: intrathecal isobaric ropivacaine 0.5% with 25 microg fentanyl
intrathecal isobaric ropivacaine 0.5% with normal saline
cohort: The study included 140 ASA I-II parturients scheduled for elective Lower Segment Caesarean Section.
finding: The combination of intrathecal isobaric ropivacaine with fentanyl provides a significantly faster onset of sensory block and a clinically relevant, though not statistically significant, prolongation of sensory block and analgesia compared to plain isobaric ropivacaine.
mod_finding: The fentanyl combination for elective Lower Segment Caesarean Section provided superior intraoperative anaesthetic parameters and a better quality of postoperative analgesia.
followup_time: immediate postoperative period (up to 120 minutes for analgesia duration)
